ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a cube net, with four connected squares horizontally; from left to right they are labeled A, B, C, D. Square E is above C, and square F is below C. The three dashed lines in the figure are respectively located on A, E, and D: the dashed line in A goes from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner, the dashed line in E goes from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner, and the dashed line in D goes from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner. Then reason: When the net is folded along C into a cube, B, D, E, and F become the four side faces around C, and A folds to the opposite side of C. After folding, the upper-right endpoint of A will coincide with the upper-left endpoint of E; the lower-left endpoint of A will coincide with the lower-right endpoint of D; the lower-right endpoint of E originally corresponds with the upper-left endpoint of D to the same cube vertex. Therefore the three dashed lines connect end to end on the surface of the cube, forming a closed three-sided boundary. Also because each dashed line is a diagonal of a square face of the same size, the lengths of the three sides are equal. Thus the shape of the cut-out hole is an equilateral triangle.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram shows a net of a cube, with three dotted lines added. If you folded the net into a cube and then cut along the dotted lines, what would be the shape of the hole?

method.method_draft: Label the four squares in the horizontal strip from left to right as A, B, C, D, with E above C and F below C. From the image, note the dotted diagonals are on A from lower-left to upper-right, on E from upper-left to lower-right, and on D from upper-left to lower-right. Fold the net mentally around square C: B, D, E, and F become the four side faces around C, and A folds over as the face opposite C. Track the endpoints of the dotted diagonals under this folding. The upper-right endpoint of A coincides with the upper-left endpoint of E; the lower-left endpoint of A coincides with the lower-right endpoint of D; and E’s lower-right endpoint is already the same cube vertex as D’s upper-left endpoint. Thus the three dotted segments join end-to-end on the cube surface to form a closed three-sided boundary. Since each segment is a diagonal of a congruent square face, all three boundary sides have equal length, so the hole is an equilateral triangle.

method.method_draft: Interpret the folded cube directly in 3D. From the image, the dotted cuts lie along diagonals of three square faces: the left end face of the strip, the top face attached above the central square, and the right face of the strip. After folding the net, these three faces are mutually adjacent around a corner pattern of the cube, and the chosen diagonals connect three alternating cube vertices. Model a cube of side length 1: each dotted segment becomes a face diagonal, so each has length sqrt(2). The three segments connect pairwise to form the triangular cross-section cut off by the plane passing through those three cube vertices. Because the three sides of this cross-section are all cube face diagonals of equal length sqrt(2), the opening is an equilateral triangle.
